The earliest human accounts are inconsistent and were often recorded generations after the landing.

No human record is old enough to preserve direct knowledge of the true origin of the Godscar.

docs.title: The Arkfall
docs.text:
The arrival of the first humans is commonly called The Arkfall.

The term refers to both the physical landing of the first ark-ships and the beginning of permanent human settlement on Arkhaven.

The first arrivals are often called the Arkborne.

Later noble houses claiming descent from the first captains, priests, and shipmasters are sometimes referred to as Arkline Houses.

The Arkfall is treated differently by different cultures.

Human states often describe it as an act of survival, courage, and divine providence.

Older established peoples and local traditions may describe it more critically, as the beginning of colonisation, displacement, and political disruption.

docs.title: Early Settlement
docs.text:
The first human settlements were established along coastlines, river mouths, sheltered bays, and fertile lowland regions.

Early communities depended heavily on:

  • Fishing
  • Ship repair
  • Coastal farming
  • Hunting
  • Trade with established local peoples
  • Salvage from the ark-ships
  • Religious organisation
  • Defensive cooperation

At first, human populations were small and vulnerable.

Their survival depended on adaptation, alliances, and access to food, timber, stone, and fresh water.

Over time, the settlements expanded inland.

docs.title: Expansion
docs.text:
Human expansion across Arkhaven occurred gradually over several centuries.

The main drivers of expansion were:

  • Population growth
  • Agricultural settlement
  • Timber demand
  • Road construction
  • Religious mission
  • Trade development
  • Territorial ambition
  • Access to mines and rivers
  • Control of strategic crossings

Humans were not stronger than every people they encountered.

They were more numerous, more expansionist, and more willing to settle contested or unstable land.

This allowed them to become the dominant population across much of the continent.

docs.title: Colonial Legacy
docs.text:
The rise of human power on Arkhaven is inseparable from colonial settlement.

Human societies often portray their history as one of survival and civilisation-building.

Many non-human cultures remember the same process as displacement, treaty-breaking, forced conversion, land seizure, cultural absorption, and exploitation.

Both views exist in the modern continent.

Many human families have now lived on Arkhaven for centuries and consider themselves fully native to the land.

At the same time, older peoples often preserve records showing that many human towns, farms, roads, and temples were built on land previously held, used, or protected by others.

This tension remains one of the major unresolved political and cultural issues in Arkhaven.

docs.title: Political Division
docs.text:
There is no single human ruler of Arkhaven.

Human populations are divided among many states and systems of government.

Common forms include:

  • Monarchies
  • Theocracies
  • Merchant republics
  • Free cities
  • Military marcher states
  • Agrarian kingdoms
  • Settler leagues
  • Noble confederations

Some rulers claim descent from the Arkborne.

Others base legitimacy on conquest, election, wealth, military control, religious authority, or popular support.

Human states frequently compete with one another for territory, trade routes, religious influence, access to rivers, and control of strategic crossings.

docs.title: Society
docs.text:
Human societies vary greatly by region.

Despite this variation, several common patterns are widespread.

Most human settlements place strong emphasis on:

  • Family inheritance
  • Land ownership
  • Written law
  • Taxation
  • Farming
  • Military service
  • Market trade
  • Religious participation
  • Civic identity

Human society is generally more mobile and less bound by ancient custom than elven or dwarven society.

This flexibility has allowed humans to adapt quickly to new regions, institutions, and political structures.

It has also made human societies prone to instability, factionalism, and rapid ideological change.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text:
Religion plays a major role in human culture.

Human churches were strongly shaped by the fact that humans arrived after the Godscar had already formed.

Because humans did not witness the original event, their religious traditions developed through interpretation, adoption, dispute, and revision.

Many human-led churches treated the Godscar as evidence that Arkhaven was divinely significant.

Some went further and argued that the arrival of the Arkborne had been foretold or divinely sanctioned.

These claims later became politically important.

Human rulers and churches often used religious authority to justify settlement, territorial claims, law, and war.

docs.title: War of the False Saints
docs.text:
Humans were major participants in War of the False Saints.

They were not the only people involved, but human-led churches and states were among the main accelerants of the conflict.

Several factors contributed to this:

  • Rapidly expanding religious institutions
  • Young and inconsistent church records
  • Political competition between human states
  • Desire for divine legitimacy
  • Use of saints and relics to justify land claims
  • Popular response to miracle claims and prophecy

The war exposed the dangers of religious ambition combined with unstable historical memory.

It also contributed directly to the later authority of The Scriptor Compact.

docs.title: Relationship with the Scriptor Compact
docs.text:
The Scriptor Compact is often viewed as a response to the instability of human religious institutions.

Many human churches accepted Scriptors because doing so provided legitimacy, continuity, and access to older records.

At the same time, many human clergy and rulers resent the influence of long-lived elven advisors within their institutions.

This creates an ongoing tension.

Human churches need Scriptor authority, but often dislike Scriptor oversight.

docs.title: Relationship with Elves
docs.text:
Human relations with Elves are complex.

Elves often view humans as impatient, expansionist, historically careless, and politically volatile.

Humans often view elves as secretive, obstructive, arrogant, and unwilling to share knowledge.

Despite this, cooperation is common.

Human rulers rely on elven scholars, translators, Scriptors, diplomats, and magical specialists.

Elven institutions often rely on human roads, trade systems, military protection, and political access.

docs.title: Relationship with Dwarves
docs.text:
Human relations with Dwarves are generally practical and economically important.

Humans rely heavily on dwarven expertise in:

  • Stonework
  • Metalwork
  • Engineering
  • Mining
  • Fortification
  • Bridge construction
  • Tunnel surveying

Disputes occur over mining rights, mountain borders, taxation, and control of trade routes.

However, human and dwarven states maintain some of the strongest economic relationships on the continent.

docs.title: Relationship with Tabaxi
docs.text:
Human relations with Tabaxi are more strained in many northern regions.

Some human traders, hunters, and criminal groups have been involved in attempts to capture young tabaxi for sale.

Many human states officially condemn such practices.

Others have failed to prevent them, ignored them, or allowed illegal markets to operate through corruption.

As a result, tabaxi communities often treat human travellers with caution until trust is earned.

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text:
Humans have a divided reputation across Arkhaven.

They are often regarded as:

  • Adaptable
  • Ambitious
  • Energetic
  • Inventive
  • Greedy
  • Expansionist
  • Brave
  • Restless
  • Politically divided
  • Religiously intense
  • Quick to build
  • Quick to justify conquest

These reputations vary by region and class.

A human farmer, sailor, saint, soldier, merchant, priest, and colonising noble may have little in common beyond shared ancestry and broad cultural inheritance.

docs.title: Strengths
docs.text:
Human strengths are generally social and institutional rather than biological.

Humans are capable of rapid organisation, settlement, alliance-building, and cultural adaptation.

They are often willing to adopt useful practices from other peoples and reshape them into human institutions.

This has made them effective builders of towns, roads, fleets, churches, armies, and states.

docs.title: Weaknesses
docs.text:
The main weaknesses of human societies are also institutional.

Human states are prone to:

  • Expansionism
  • Religious certainty
  • Historical revision
  • Political factionalism
  • Short-term ambition
  • Resource exploitation
  • Border conflict
  • Justification of conquest

Their shorter lives and fast political cycles make long-term memory difficult to preserve without archives, law, or outside institutions.

docs.title: Current Status
docs.text:
Humans are now the dominant population across much of Arkhaven.

They control many of the continent’s largest cities, farmland regions, trade routes, ports, churches, and armies.

However, their power is fragmented.

No single human state controls the continent, and human rulers are often as dangerous to one another as they are to neighbouring peoples.

Their history remains politically contested.

To many humans, they are the descendants of desperate survivors who crossed the sea and built a new home.

To many older peoples, they are settlers who became rulers and then wrote the map in their own language.

The central human legacy in Arkhaven is therefore one of survival becoming entitlement.

docs.title: Tabaxi
docs.text:
Tabaxi are a feline humanoid people found primarily in the northern territories of Arkhaven, especially within the tropical rainforest, dense jungle, river basin, and coastal forest regions.

They are widely known for their agility, curiosity, oral traditions, sharp senses, and ability to move through difficult forest terrain with unusual speed and confidence.

In Lazuril, tabaxi culture is strongly shaped by the northern jungle environment, treetop settlement, trade secrecy, sign language, and a long history of avoiding capture by outside hunters and slavers.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Tabaxi are an intelligent and highly mobile people with feline features, including fur, claws, tails, reflective eyes, and strong climbing ability.

They are not a single unified nation.

Most tabaxi communities are organised into kin-groups, travelling bands, treetop settlements, river clans, shrine families, and loose regional confederations.

Tabaxi culture values:

  • Freedom of movement
  • Curiosity
  • Personal reputation
  • Family protection
  • Storytelling
  • Skilled hunting
  • Silent travel
  • Trade knowledge
  • Memory of routes
  • Resistance to captivity

Their societies tend to be flexible rather than centralised.

docs.title: Geographic Distribution
docs.text:
The largest tabaxi populations live in the northern jungles and rainforests of Arkhaven.

These regions are hot, humid, densely vegetated, and difficult for outsiders to navigate.

Tabaxi settlements are most commonly found in:

  • High canopy regions
  • River valleys
  • Rainforest interiors
  • Coastal jungle belts
  • Hidden ravines
  • Giant tree clusters
  • Forested cliffs
  • Wetland margins

Smaller tabaxi communities also exist near trade routes, port settlements, and frontier towns, though many avoid permanent residence in heavily populated human regions.

docs.title: Historical Position
docs.text:
Tabaxi communities were established in the northern forests before the expansion of major human states.

Their own traditions do not claim direct knowledge of the true origin of The Godscar. Like other peoples of modern Arkhaven, they preserve theories, stories, and religious interpretations rather than direct memory of the event.

The arrival and later expansion of Humans changed tabaxi relations with the wider continent.

Some human settlements became trade partners. Others became sources of danger, especially where hunters, traffickers, or frontier markets sought to capture young tabaxi.

docs.title: Treetop Settlements
docs.text:
Most established tabaxi homes are built within the upper canopy.

These settlements may include:

  • Rope bridges
  • Hidden platforms
  • Suspended huts
  • Woven walkways
  • Tree-hollow stores
  • Rain collectors
  • Climbing routes
  • Lookout perches
  • Concealed nursery spaces

Treetop construction provides protection from ground predators, flooding, raiders, and hunters.

The highest and most concealed areas of a settlement are usually reserved for children, elders, food stores, and signal keepers.

Outsiders rarely see a complete tabaxi settlement.

Visitors are often received on lower platforms or forest-floor meeting grounds rather than being allowed into the upper dwellings.

docs.title: Predators and Captivity
docs.text:
Tabaxi communities have a long history of defending themselves against predators, raiders, and those who attempt to capture young tabaxi for sale.

This has made settlement secrecy a cultural necessity.

Tabaxi children are carefully protected, and most communities maintain strict rules regarding:

  • Outsider access
  • Camp locations
  • Travel routes
  • Night movement
  • Firelight use
  • Trade negotiation
  • Stranger contact
  • Child movement outside the canopy

Slave-taking is treated as one of the most serious crimes by tabaxi communities.

Families and neighbouring clans may cooperate across large distances to recover captured children or punish known traffickers.

docs.title: Common Sign Language
docs.text:
Tabaxi in Arkhaven commonly learn Common Sign Language.

This practice developed for several reasons:

  • Silent hunting
  • Avoiding predators
  • Coordination during travel
  • Trade with outsiders
  • Communication when speech would reveal position
  • Protection during raids or pursuit

Most tabaxi children learn signs before they are considered safe to travel beyond the immediate settlement.

Sign language is also important during inter-clan meetings, negotiations, and watchkeeping.

Many tabaxi can communicate across reasonable distance using subtle hand, tail, ear, and body movements combined with formal sign.

docs.title: Language and Storytelling
docs.text:
Tabaxi language traditions are strongly oral.

Stories are used to preserve:

  • Routes
  • Warnings
  • Clan memory
  • Hunting knowledge
  • Moral lessons
  • Trade history
  • Family lineages
  • Encounters with outsiders

Tabaxi often treat stories as practical tools rather than entertainment alone.

A story may encode the location of a safe crossing, the habits of a dangerous beast, or the identity of a trader who cannot be trusted.

Written records exist, but they are less central than memory, song, rhythm, gesture, and repeated performance.

docs.title: Curiosity and Travel
docs.text:
Tabaxi are widely associated with curiosity.

This trait is often misunderstood by outsiders as restlessness or lack of seriousness.

Among tabaxi, curiosity is considered a survival skill.

A person who notices unusual tracks, strange smells, altered bird calls, broken vines, or unfamiliar trade goods may prevent disaster.

Many tabaxi leave their home regions for a time to gather stories, maps, objects, debts, songs, and news.

Some return home after years of travel.

Others become permanent wanderers, guides, merchants, scouts, performers, or adventurers.

docs.title: Trade
docs.text:
Tabaxi trade exists, but it is cautious and selective.

Common trade goods include:

  • Rare fruits
  • Medicinal plants
  • Dyes
  • Feathers
  • Carved wood
  • Jungle resins
  • Spices
  • Animal products
  • Route knowledge
  • Fine woven goods

Tabaxi are often reluctant to sell detailed maps of their homeland.

They may trade guidance, but rarely surrender full knowledge of hidden paths, settlement locations, or canopy routes.

docs.title: Religion and Belief
docs.text:
Tabaxi religious practice varies between communities.

Common religious themes include:

  • Freedom
  • Fortune
  • Moonlight
  • Hunting
  • Stories
  • Ancestral memory
  • Forest spirits
  • Protection of children
  • Respect for dangerous places

Many tabaxi communities maintain small shrines in tree hollows, cliff shelters, or concealed groves.

Rituals are often brief, mobile, and woven into daily life rather than centred on large formal temples.

docs.title: Relationship with Other Peoples
docs.text:
Tabaxi relations with other peoples are shaped by caution.

They are not hostile by default, but most communities judge outsiders by action rather than stated intent.

Positive relationships are most common with:

  • Honest traders
  • River guides
  • Healers
  • Scholars who respect boundaries
  • Anti-slavery groups
  • Forest communities

Relations are poor with groups known for hunting, trafficking, forced labour, or exploitative trade.

Some human and coastal settlements have long-standing agreements with nearby tabaxi clans.

Other regions are avoided entirely.

docs.title: Warfare and Defence
docs.text:
Tabaxi warfare is usually defensive, mobile, and terrain-focused.

Common tactics include:

  • Ambush
  • Night movement
  • Canopy travel
  • Silent signalling
  • Trap use
  • Hit-and-run attacks
  • Misdirection
  • Evacuation routes
  • Rescue raids

Tabaxi rarely favour direct battlefield confrontation unless forced.

Their greatest military advantage is their ability to move through jungle terrain faster and more quietly than most enemies.

Settlements are designed with layered escape routes rather than only fixed defences.

docs.title: Reputation in Arkhaven
docs.text:
Tabaxi have a mixed reputation across Arkhaven.

They are often described as:

  • Curious
  • Agile
  • Secretive
  • Difficult to track
  • Skilled climbers
  • Excellent scouts
  • Unpredictable traders
  • Protective of children
  • Distrustful of authority

Some of these views are accurate.

Others are shaped by outsiders who do not understand tabaxi caution or who resent being denied access to northern forest routes.

docs.title: Current Status
docs.text:
Tabaxi communities remain strongest in the northern jungles and rainforests.

Their settlements are rarely marked accurately on outside maps.

Their people continue to play an important role as guides, scouts, traders, storytellers, messengers, and defenders of northern forest routes.

Although some tabaxi now live in cities or travel widely across Lazuril, most remain culturally tied to the canopy settlements and hidden communities of the northern territories.

Their central political concern remains unchanged: survival without captivity, trade without exposure, and freedom without surrendering the safety of their young.

docs.title: Lazuril
docs.text:
Lazuril is the known world upon which the continent of Arkhaven exists.

The world is dominated by vast oceans, separated continental landmasses, deep climatic variation, ancient religious history, and long-lived civilisations whose records often contradict one another.

The name "Lazuril" is commonly associated with the blue appearance of the world when viewed through astronomical instruments or described in older cosmological writings.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Lazuril contains multiple continents, major ocean systems, isolated island chains, polar regions, and large unexplored territories.

Only portions of the world are well documented.

Most surviving historical records originate from:

  • Arkhaven
  • Elven archive houses
  • Dwarven engineering records
  • Religious institutions
  • Maritime trade powers

Large sections of the world remain poorly mapped.

docs.title: Astronomy
docs.text:
The study of astronomy is practiced by scholars, navigators, Scriptors, sailors, and religious observatories throughout Lazuril.

Several major cultures maintain differing cosmological models regarding:

  • The movement of celestial bodies
  • The divine structure of the heavens
  • The origins of the world
  • The role of magic in the cosmos
  • The relationship between the gods and the stars

Astronomical observation is especially important for navigation and calendar keeping.

docs.title: Continents
docs.text:
Arkhaven is currently the best documented continent in surviving records.

Other continental landmasses are known to exist beyond the surrounding seas, though many remain politically or geographically distant from the affairs of Arkhaven.

Some are known primarily through:

  • Merchant records
  • Sailor testimony
  • Pilgrimage accounts
  • Diplomatic reports
  • Fragmentary maps
  • Ancient archive references

docs.title: Oceans and Seas
docs.text:
The oceans of Lazuril are major drivers of trade, migration, climate, and political influence.

Long-distance travel remains dangerous due to:

  • Storm systems
  • Sea monsters
  • Navigational uncertainty
  • Piracy
  • Uncharted waters
  • Seasonal currents

Despite this, maritime trade connects large parts of the known world.

docs.title: Historical Ages
docs.text:
Most historians divide the history of Lazuril into broad historical ages.

Exact dates remain disputed.

Major eras commonly referenced include:

  • The Age Before Memory
  • The Age of Fracture
  • The Post-Godscar Era
  • The Era of Silence
  • The Age of False Saints
  • The Compact Era

These classifications are used differently between cultures and institutions.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text:
Religion is one of the defining forces of Lazuril.

The gods are widely accepted as real entities capable of interacting with the mortal world through divine magic, prophecy, visions, omens, and miracles.

At the same time, the history of Lazuril demonstrates that divine claims can be manipulated, misunderstood, or falsified.

This tension heavily influences politics, scholarship, and law.

docs.title: Current Status
docs.text:
Lazuril remains politically fragmented and historically incomplete.

Ancient ruins, disputed records, forgotten roads, submerged structures, and lost civilisations continue to shape the modern world.

Many scholars believe significant portions of Lazurilian history remain undiscovered, concealed, or deliberately restricted.
